description: WHEN DFHRESP(DUPKEY) and WHEN DFHRESP(DUPREC) of the ordered EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD in WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:510-547 - the TWO STACKED CLAUSES at :533 and :534 that share ONE body at :535-539 - and, reached through them, THE SHARPEST CONSEQUENCE THE UNGUARDED PAYMENT BLOCK HAS: THE TRANSACTION IS REFUSED AND THE BALANCE IS DEBITED ANYWAY. SERVICE, driving billing.BillPaymentService.processEnterKey directly through its own constructor: no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no WebTestClient, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no ApplicationContext anywhere in the path, because that is where the decision logic lives and a parity case must reach it with nothing in between (gate G51). THE HEADLINE - A REJECTED WRITE STILL PAYS THE BILL. :208 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON is the ONLY guard in the payment sequence and it is evaluated BEFORE the block is entered. Once inside, :210 IF CONF-PAY-YES opens a straight run of statements - :211 PERFORM READ-CXACAIX-FILE, :212 MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID, :213 PERFORM STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE, :214 PERFORM READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE, :215 PERFORM ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE, :216 MOVE TRAN-ID TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM, :217 ADD 1 TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM, :218 INITIALIZE TRAN-RECORD, :219-229 the eleven moves, :230 PERFORM GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP, :231-232 the one MOVE with two timestamp receivers, :233 PERFORM WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE, :234 COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT and :235 PERFORM UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE - and THERE IS NO SECOND IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON ANYWHERE BETWEEN :211 AND :235. So the duplicate arm at :535-539 raises WS-ERR-FLG, moves its message, repositions the cursor and TRANSMITS A REJECTION - and then :234 subtracts the payment from the balance and :235 rewrites the account, even though NO TRANSACT ROW WAS ADDED. The customer's balance is reduced to zero with no transaction record anywhere to justify the reduction. That is genuine legacy behaviour and it is preserved exactly (practice B5): no early return is inserted after the failed write, the COMPUTE is not skipped, the rewrite is not suppressed, and none of it is treated as a defect to be corrected. A plausible-looking Java translation would NATURALLY return after a refused write and would then leave the balance unchanged - which is precisely why expectedWrites below asserts the rewritten account row POSITIVELY while asserting NO transaction row at all. If this file's ACCTDAT expectation were ever softened to the seeded balance, a guard that does not exist would have been modelled (gate G28). HOW THE ARM IS INDUCED, AND WHY THE COLLISION IS REAL RATHER THAN STIPULATED. The declared forcing is forcedOutcomes.write with outcome DUPLICATE, which the gate's service adapter translates into TransactionRepository.WriteResult.duplicate(TRANSACT) - FileStatus.DUPLICATE '22', Outcome.DUPLICATE, and the CICS response CicsResponse.of(FileStatus.DUPREC), which is 14. But the forcing is not an assertion pulled out of the air: THE SEEDED MASTER GENUINELY ALREADY HOLDS THE KEY THIS INVOCATION COMPUTES, and the arithmetic that gets there is stated here in full so a reader can check it. :212 moves HIGH-VALUES into TRAN-ID, which is how CICS is told to position past the last record, so the backward browse at :213-215 returns the HIGHEST existing identifier. TRANSACT is seeded with two rows in ascending key order and the highest is '9999999999999999' - numerically the highest, and also the last row seeded, so a real VSAM backward browse and this gate's stub agree on which row is returned rather than merely happening to coincide. :216 MOVE TRAN-ID TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM moves that X(16) image into PIC 9(16) at equal width, so no digit is lost. :217 ADD 1 TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM then increments a receiver that is ALREADY AT SIXTEEN NINES, and the statement carries NO ON SIZE ERROR CLAUSE, so the seventeen-digit sum discards its HIGH-ORDER digit and WRAPS TO '0000000000000000' - a numeric receiver is aligned on its implied decimal point, so the digits that survive a cross-width numeric store are the LOW-order ones, and keeping the leading digits instead is the classic defect. That wrapped identifier is the key of the OTHER seeded row, so :233 offers the cluster a key it already contains and a real KSDS answers DUPREC. THE WRAPAROUND IS THIS FILE'S OWN GROUND: sibling case18 exercises a carry across two digit columns - ninety-nine to one hundred - and says in terms that a receiver already at sixteen nines is 'not this case'; case15 goes seven to eight and case16 goes from an empty master to one. None of them reaches the wrap, and this file does. WHAT THE TWO STACKED CLAUSES CAN AND CANNOT BE TOLD APART BY, STATED HONESTLY. :533 WHEN DFHRESP(DUPKEY) and :534 WHEN DFHRESP(DUPREC) are two clause labels above ONE shared body at :535-539, and that body is four statements - MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG, MOVE 'Tran ID already exist...' TO WS-MESSAGE, MOVE -1 TO ACTIDINL, PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN - none of which is a DISPLAY and none of which reads WS-RESP-CD. So NOTHING AT THE OBSERVABLE BOUNDARY DISTINGUISHES THE TWO CLAUSES: whichever label matched, the emissions, the message, the cursor, the send count and both dataset channels are identical. This one invocation therefore exercises the complete observable content of both clauses, and that is the honest claim rather than a claim to have driven two distinct labels. The repository layer makes the same point independently: FileStatus maps DUPREC 14 and DUPKEY 15 FORWARD onto the same batch status '22', and cicsRespOfBatchStatus deliberately declines to map '22' back, because the reverse is genuinely ambiguous - so a duplicate reported through the batch status cannot be resolved to one of the two CICS responses at all. Gate G30 is satisfied for the site as a whole: the source order is NORMAL at :523, DUPKEY at :533, DUPREC at :534 and WHEN OTHER at :540, WHEN OTHER IS LAST, and the DFHRESP(NORMAL) test that had to fail first is asserted here and not merely traversed - a restructuring that hoisted WHEN OTHER above the duplicate clauses would report 'Unable to Add Bill pay Transaction...' where the program reports 'Tran ID already exist...'. WHICH ARMS THIS FILE COVERS, WHICH SIBLINGS COVER, AND WHICH CANNOT BE COVERED FROM A CASE FILE AT ALL. A ParityCase carries one screenRequest, which is one invocation, and each of these paragraphs issues its CICS command once per invocation, so one arm per site per file is forced by the model rather than chosen. WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE at :510-547: DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :523-532 is covered by case15, case16 and case18; the DUPKEY/DUPREC body at :533-539 is COVERED HERE and by no sibling; WHEN OTHER at :540-546 IS NOT COVERED BY THIS FILE AND IS NOT COVERED BY case01 THROUGH case18, so gate G47 for that arm is not satisfied until a sibling adopts it, and its shape is fully determined so whichever sibling takes it has an exact contract - seed exactly as this file seeds, declare forcedOutcomes.write with any outcome OTHER THAN DUPLICATE (the adapter answers WriteResult.other(TRANSACT, FileStatus.RECORD_LENGTH_CONFLICT), whose '04' has no CICS counterpart), and then :541 DISPLAY emits one line, :542 raises the flag, :543-544 moves 'Unable to Add Bill pay Transaction...' - thirty-seven characters, capital Add, 'Bill pay' as two words with a lower-case pay, capital Transaction, exactly three trailing dots - :545 positions the cursor and :546 sends, after which :234 and :235 run exactly as they run here. STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :441-467 and READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE at :472-496 ARE A DIFFERENT AND HARDER CASE, AND THE OBSTRUCTION IS RECORDED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND. Their DFHRESP(NORMAL) arms - :452-453 and :485-486 - are covered here and by case15 and case18, and READPREV's DFHRESP(ENDFILE) arm at :487-488, which moves ZEROS to TRAN-ID and IS NOT AN ERROR, is covered by case16 and is deliberately not duplicated here. But STARTBR's DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :454-459, STARTBR's WHEN OTHER at :460-466 and READPREV's WHEN OTHER at :489-495 CANNOT BE INDUCED FROM A CASE FILE AS THE GATE'S SERVICE ADAPTER STANDS, and that is a property of the adapter and not of this expectation: the browse is positioned with the compile-time constant BillPaymentService.STARTBR_POSITIONING_OUTCOME, which is Outcome.OK, so no declared input reaches the other two arms; the backward read is derived purely from the seeded rows, empty answering ENDFILE and non-empty answering the highest row, so no declared input reaches its WHEN OTHER; and the harness REFUSES a run whose declared forcing never fired, so naming startBrowse or readNext in forcedOutcomes would fail the run for an unconsumed forcing rather than reach the arm. Their shapes are nevertheless fully determined from the source, so nothing is lost but the execution: :454-459 raises the flag, moves 'Transaction ID NOT found...' - twenty-seven characters, capital NOT, exactly three trailing dots - repositions the cursor and sends; :460-466 and :489-495 both DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD first and then move THE SAME LITERAL, 'Unable to lookup Transaction...', thirty-one characters - so THOSE TWO CALL SITES EMIT BYTE-IDENTICAL TEXT AND ARE DISTINGUISHABLE ONLY BY THEIR SIDE EFFECTS, exactly as :361, :392 and :425 are for 'Account ID NOT found...'; and in READPREV's WHEN OTHER, TRAN-ID is still the sixteen X'FF' bytes :212 put there when :216 moves it into a PIC 9(16) counter, which raises a data exception on z/OS - S0C7 - so the task abends without writing anything, and the codec's refusal of a non-digit image is the faithful Java counterpart. ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE AT :501-505 HAS NO ARM AND NONE IS INVENTED. It is a BARE EXEC CICS ENDBR with NO RESP and NO RESP2 option and therefore no EVALUATE after it, so it can report nothing and is asserted as reporting nothing (practice B5). THE FIELDS THE FAILURE ARM DOES NOT BLANK, WHICH IS BEHAVIOUR AND IS ASSERTED AS SUCH. PERFORM INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS lives at :524, on the write's DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm ONLY, and the duplicate body at :535-539 does not perform it. So ACTIDINI, CURBALI, CONFIRMI and WS-MESSAGE are NOT blanked and NOT re-initialised on this path: ACTIDINO carries the identifier exactly as received, CONFIRMO carries the confirmation flag exactly as received, and CURBALO carries the edited balance - because :193-194 sit inside the :169 block and run BEFORE :208, so the balance was moved into WS-CURR-BAL PIC +9999999999.99 and thence into CURBALI long before the write was attempted. That is the opposite of the success path, where all three come back blank, and it is the difference a translation that reused the success arm's tidy-up would erase. Sibling case18 recorded that its first send was the only populated CURBALO in this directory; that was true when it was written, and this file adds two more for the same sequencing reason - the observation is left where it stands rather than edited, because a sibling case file is not this file's to change (practices B3, B4). TWO SENDS, AND THE LAST WRITER WINS - WHICH HERE MEANS THE REJECTION WINS. The send count is itself behaviour: a clean payment sends twice, a rejection before the guard sends once, and this path sends twice with BOTH sends carrying the refusal. FIRST, :539 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN from the shared duplicate body. SECOND, :235 UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE takes its own DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm at :388-389, which emits nothing at all, and then :242 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN - unconditional within the :208 block - sends again. Nothing between the two assigns a new message, so the second send carries the same text as the first; that is 'the last assignment to WS-MESSAGE before the last send wins' producing the rejection rather than, as in case18, burying it. Every screen message is moved into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) at :39 and then right-truncated into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) at :293, so each ERRMSGO here is 'Tran ID already exist...' - TWENTY-FOUR characters, note 'Tran' and not 'Transaction', and 'exist' and NOT 'exists' - left-justified and space-filled to exactly seventy-eight. WHY expectedMessages IS EMPTY, AND WHY THAT IS AN ASSERTION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Of the six DISPLAY sites in this program - :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541 - not one is on this path. The duplicate body has no DISPLAY, and every other paragraph this invocation reaches takes its DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm: the account read at :357-358, the cross-reference read at :421-422, the browse start at :452-453, the backward read at :485-486 and the rewrite at :388-389. So the unit emits no line at all, and an empty expectedMessages positively states that - emission count is compared before emission content, so a translation that added a diagnostic on the duplicate arm would fail on the count. THE DISPLAY RENDERING CONVENTION IS SIBLING case17's AND IS RESTATED RATHER THAN RE-INVENTED, then applied by NOT applying it, exactly as case18 does: the four operands of DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD concatenate with NO separator, WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD are both PIC S9(09) COMP at :46-47 and render UNSIGNED and ZERO-FILLED at exactly nine digit positions, so the line is always 5 + 9 + 5 + 9 = 28 characters, and a code with no CICS value to report renders as NINE ASTERISKS rather than nine zeros because zero IS DFHRESP(NORMAL). The WS-MESSAGE text is not restated as a WS_MESSAGE_80 entry either: the screen is where this program's message becomes observable and ERRMSGO is pinned in the sends below, stating it in both places would create two opinions about one value, and the two channels have different widths - eighty against seventy-eight - so they are not interchangeable. THE ARITHMETIC - TRUNCATION, NOT ROUNDING, AND NAMED EXPLICITLY. The seeded account carries ACCT-CURR-BAL PIC S9(10)V99 as the twelve-byte zoned image '00000002530{', where the trailing '{' is the standard positive sign overpunch for a low-order digit zero: ten integer digits, two fraction digits, value 253.00. :224 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO TRAN-AMT is a CROSS-WIDTH NUMERIC MOVE into PIC S9(09)V99, and a numeric receiver aligns on its IMPLIED DECIMAL POINT, so the digit that does not fit is the HIGH-ORDER one and never a fraction digit. Here that digit is zero, so the move is lossless and TRAN-AMT holds the eleven-byte image '0000002530{'; the LOSSY variant of this same move, where a balance needing ten integer digits loses its leading digit, is sibling case20's job and is not restated here. :234 COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT then subtracts exactly, and the two operands are equal, so the residual is exactly 0.00 and the receiver holds '00000000000{' - the ONLY field of the three-hundred-byte record that changes. Every value is held as BigDecimal at THE SCALE ITS PICTURE DECLARES - SCALE 2 for both spans (gate G23) - and never as double or float, which cannot represent a COBOL PIC S9(n)V99 exactly (rule R4, gate G22). Every store TRUNCATES with ROUNDINGMODE.DOWN, because the keyword ROUNDED appears ZERO TIMES across all twenty-eight programs and :234 carries none: HALF_UP, HALF_EVEN, CEILING and FLOOR are all wrong here and none appears (rule R2, gate G24). No COMP-3 exists in ANY of the twenty-eight copybooks - verified zero - so no persisted field needs packed-decimal unpacking, and this program's one COMP-3 item, WS-ABS-TIME PIC S9(15) COMP-3 at :59, never leaves memory. All record images are read and compared as US-ASCII, named explicitly in screenRequest and never left to a platform default (practice B8). THE REWRITTEN ACCOUNT, FIELD BY FIELD. The thirteen spans are summed mechanically from app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy and never counted by eye (practice B11): ACCT-ID 9(11) + ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) + ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 + ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99 + ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT S9(10)V99 + ACCT-OPEN-DATE X(10) + ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) + ACCT-REISSUE-DATE X(10) + ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT S9(10)V99 + ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT S9(10)V99 + ACCT-ADDR-ZIP X(10) + ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) + FILLER X(178) = 300 (gate G19). ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE IS MISSPELLED IN THE COPYBOOK at line 11 and is misspelled here too (requirement I1): correcting it to ACCT-EXPIRATION-DATE would leave the diff looking for a field the decoder never produces, which is a silent parity break rather than a loud one. FILLER X(178) is one hundred and seventy-eight SPACES and is EMITTED rather than omitted (gate G21) - a record missing it is 122 bytes, and expectedBytes pins the full 300 precisely so that omission fails on width. ACCT-ADDR-ZIP is 'A000000000' at offsets 103-112 and ACCT-GROUP-ID is ten spaces at 113-122, both exactly as the fixture holds them. Everything except ACCT-CURR-BAL is byte-identical to the seeded row, which is what makes 'the payment debited the balance and touched nothing else' an assertion rather than an assumption; note in particular that :234-235 does NOT zero the two cycle amounts, so ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT keep their seeded '00000000000{' images because that is what they already held and not because anything cleared them - unlike CBACT04C's account break, which does clear them. THE TRANSACTION CHANNEL IS OPENED AND EMPTY, WHICH IS ALSO A POSITIVE STATEMENT. :233 assembles a complete 350-byte TRAN-RECORD and offers it, and the cluster refuses it, so the writes channel reports the write as ISSUED AND NOT LANDED rather than as never attempted: expectedWrites carries NO TRANSACT entry and expectedDatasets declares TRANSACT WRITES at rowCount 0 with recordLength 350. An omitted channel says nothing; an empty one asserts that the WRITE was issued and did not land. expectedFinalState then carries the two seeded rows UNCHANGED and nothing else - the master is exactly as it was - while ACCTDAT's final state carries the debited row. That pairing, one dataset untouched and the other modified by the very statement the untouched one refused, IS the defect this case exists to pin. THE SEEDED MASTER, AND WHY ITS ROWS CARRY NOTHING BUT THEIR KEYS. TRANSACT has NO ASCII fixture - app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files and none of them is a transaction master - so its rows are declared INLINE at 350 bytes from app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, and no tenth fixture file is requested. Both rows are in the shape INITIALIZE leaves behind, which is also the shape sibling case15 and sibling case18 seed: the PIC X spans and the trailing FILLER space-filled, the three numeric spans zero-filled with TRAN-AMT as the zoned '0000000000{'. That is deliberate and sufficient rather than lazy - the program reads exactly two things from this dataset, the highest key at :214 and the presence of the computed key at :233, so a row that asserts only its key asserts everything the program consults, and inventing populated merchant and timestamp data would be inventing input the case does not need. THE ACCOUNT AND THE CROSS-REFERENCE ARE SEEDED FROM THE REAL FIXTURES. ACCTDAT is one row, fixtures/acctdata.txt ROW 33, byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt at exactly three hundred bytes, and ACTIDINI is '00000000034', the ACCT-ID that row carries, so the keyed read at :345-354 takes its DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm and ACCOUNT-RECORD is genuinely filled; the read is issued WITH UPDATE at :351, so its Java counterpart is readForUpdate and not a plain read, and it runs inside the unit of work the service opens. The row is chosen for independence as well: no sibling seeds fixture row 33, so the :224 move and the :234 COMPUTE here are a fresh instance rather than a restatement of case15's or case18's. CXACAIX is one row, fixtures/cardxref.txt ROW 18, which is the row whose XREF-ACCT-ID is '00000000034' - derived by slicing the fixture on the eleven-byte account key rather than by assuming an ordering, because THE FIXTURE IS KEYED BY XREF-CARD-NUM ASCENDING AND NOT BY ACCOUNT ID, so row 18 rather than row 33 is the account's row and an index assumed from the account row number would silently read another customer's card. The card number that row carries is left in the fixture rather than restated here, both because Redaction classifies a card identifier as IDENTIFIER and never renders one verbatim and because this path writes no transaction row for it to reach. Its rows measure THIRTY-SIX bytes where app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares FIFTY - XREF-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) + XREF-CUST-ID PIC 9(09) + XREF-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) + FILLER PIC X(14) - because the fixture omits that trailing FILLER, and THE FIXTURE IS LEFT EXACTLY AS IT IS (gate G16, risk R-F, practice B3): normalisations declares CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 for CXACAIX and ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow remains the SOLE owner of the 36-to-50 right pad. Nothing is pre-padded, and no fixture is edited to engineer the duplicate - the collision is engineered entirely from inline TRANSACT rows. GATE G45 - THE ALTERNATE INDEX IS A FINDER, NEVER A SECOND TABLE, AND THIS PATH TRAVERSES IT. app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines CXACAIX as a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster, one dataset with two access paths, and in Java that is CardXrefRepository.readByAccountIdViaAltIndex - a second finder method on the base repository keyed on the eleven-byte XREF-ACCT-ID, with no second repository, table, entity or index created for it, which is also why no DDL exists anywhere in the module (gate G44). The read at :410-418 carries NO UPDATE option, so it takes no lock: the cross-reference is consulted for a card number and is never written by this program. CONFIRMI IS 'Y' BY DELIBERATE CHOICE: it puts the invocation on the confirmed-payment branch at :174-177, which is the only branch that sets CONF-PAY-YES and therefore the only one from which :210 can open the payment block at all. A blank or absent confirmation reaches the account read and stops at :237-239 with 'Confirm to make a bill payment...', and the seeded balance of 253.00 is comfortably above zero so the nothing-to-pay guard at :197-206 does not fire either; both of those refusals are other cases' ground and neither is reached here. DETERMINISM. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32 - the same instant as every other case in this directory and the instant in the source's own version footer at :571 - and it is INJECTED into the service, never read from the host (practice B7). :251-253 EXEC CICS ASKTIME and :255-261 EXEC CICS FORMATTIME YYYYMMDD DATESEP('-') TIME TIMESEP(':') produce ten characters and eight; :263 INITIALIZE WS-TIMESTAMP zeroes the group's numeric items and LEAVES ITS SEPARATOR FILLERS AT THEIR DECLARED VALUES, so byte 11 stays a space and BYTE 20 STAYS A FULL STOP; :264 moves the date into bytes 1-10, :265 the time into bytes 12-19, and :266 MOVE ZEROS TO WS-TIMESTAMP-TM-MS6 fills bytes 21-26 with six zeros, giving '2022-07-19 23:12:32.000000' - twenty-six bytes, moved identically into TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS by the single MOVE with two receivers at :231-232, because this program has no separate processing instant. That timestamp is assembled on this path and then discarded with the refused record, so it appears in no expectation here; it is documented because the value must come from the fixed injected instant and never from a captured now. Nothing else in this file is environment-dependent: there is no DISPLAY to render, the seeded rows are fixture bytes and inline bytes, and the identifier arithmetic is integer. STATELESSNESS. termination is RETURN_TRANSID because :146-149 EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is where this path ends: the pseudo-conversation continues and the communication area travels in the payload, which is where statelessness is asserted rather than asserted about - the sixteen navigation spans are comparable precisely because no server-side session holds them (rule R6, gate G37). cursorField is ACTIDINL, placed there by :538. The header items POPULATE-HEADER-INFO writes at :319-338 - TRNNAMEO, TITLE01O, CURDATEO, PGMNAMEO, TITLE02O and CURTIMEO - are the controller's projection and a SERVICE case does not claim them; nextProgram, nextMapset and nextMap are absent for the same reason, since the two XCTL sites at :281-284 are performed only from MAIN-PARA and naming a target from a service invocation would claim a transfer that did not happen. ATTRIBUTES, AND WHAT IS NOT THERE. attributes is EMPTY on both sends, and that is an assertion. MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :526 is the ONLY attribute assignment in all 572 lines and it sits on the write's DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm, so a refused write never reaches it - a translation that highlighted the rejection green, or that left a highlight set from a previous state, would fail here (gate G38). DFHBMSCA is IBM-supplied and is ABSENT FROM THIS REPOSITORY (risk R-D), so the constant is reproduced in common.BmsAttributes from IBM CICS documentation; it is highlight METADATA and not a payload field. There is NO CSSETATY error highlight and NO DFHRED anywhere on this path or any other in this program: COBIL00C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY, and the literal DFHRED does not appear in its 572 lines, so the MOVE -1 into ACTIDINL at :538 is the only emphasis the rejecting arm applies and the mapset's own COLOR=RED on the ERRMSG field in app/bms/COBIL00.bms stands unaltered. NOT APPLICABLE ON THIS PATH - DO NOT INVENT. There is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in COBIL00C and the identifier RETURN-CODE does not appear in its 572 lines either, so expectedReturnCode is 0 as a POSITIVE STATEMENT about a path that both fails and completes, and not as a defaulted value - the member is boxed in the model precisely so an omitted key cannot bind to zero by accident (gate G35 does not apply). G32 does not apply because the program contains no GO TO. G39 does not apply because it paginates nothing. G40 does not apply because no XCTL is reached from the service. No ENDBR RESP arm exists to cover, because the source declares none. PROVENANCE - STATICALLY DERIVED, NOT CAPTURED. Every expected value in this file was derived by READING app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:208-244, :249-267, :289-301, :343-372, :377-403, :408-436, :441-467, :472-496, :501-505 and :510-547 against app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY, app/bms/COBIL00.bms and the real fixture rows of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt and app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt - and NONE OF IT WAS CAPTURED FROM A LIVE COBOL EXECUTION. Executing the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment: no z/OS runtime and no CICS emulator is available, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled and provides no Language Environment CEE services, and the IBM-supplied copybooks DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR that these programs include are absent from the repository - eight independently verified blockers in total. That substitution is recorded as risk R-A and it changes THE PROVENANCE OF THE EXPECTED VALUES AND NOTHING ELSE: the twenty cases per program, the field-by-field diffing and the diff-count-must-be-zero-per-module gate all stand unchanged. Read this expectation as a careful reading of the source, which is what it is, and not as a recording of a run. Three of its statements are interpretations rather than transcriptions and all three are flagged where they occur: that DUPKEY and DUPREC are indistinguishable at the observable boundary and are therefore covered as one shared body rather than as two driven labels; that the STARTBR NOTFND, STARTBR WHEN OTHER and READPREV WHEN OTHER arms cannot be induced from a case file as the gate's adapter stands, so their shapes are documented and left for a sibling or an adapter extension; and that the duplicate this case turns on is induced through a declared forcing whose corresponding real condition - the computed key already present in the seeded master - is constructed to be genuine rather than merely asserted. GATES: G15, G16 with the real unpadded acctdata.txt and cardxref.txt both left untouched, G18, G19 at 350 and 300 with the cross-reference's 50 declared through the pad, G21 for both FILLER spans, G22, G23, G24, G28 as the PRIMARY gate for the COMPUTE that runs on a rejected write, G30, G37, G38 with no highlight on a refused write, G44, G45, G47 as the PRIMARY gate for the DUPKEY/DUPREC arm of the WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE call site, and G51. Rules R1, R2, R4, R5, R6 and R7 and requirement I1 all govern this file; review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', so NO USER RULE DOES - and per the plan's own reading that is not licence to lower the bar, so practices B1, B3, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 are held in its place.
